cases.question: How did Anton Bacaj describe AI engineering to the author?
cases.answer: He said AI engineering is just software engineering with AI models thrown in the stack.

evidence.quote: Anton Bacaj told me that “AI engineering is just software engineering with AI models thrown in the stack.”

cases.question: According to the book, how many epochs of data are large models typically pre-trained on?
cases.answer: As of the book's writing, large models are typically pre-trained on only one epoch of data.

evidence.quote: As of this writing, large models are typically pre-trained on only one epoch of data.

cases.question: Why does the author warn against comparing Azure AI Studio's relevance scores with MLflow's relevance scores?
cases.answer: Because AI-as-a-judge criteria aren't standardized; the scores depend on each judge's underlying model and prompt, so they can be very different.

evidence.quote: It’s essential to remember that AI as a judge criteria aren’t standardized. Azure AI Studio’s relevance scores might be very different from MLflow’s relevance scores. These scores depend on the judge’s underlying model and prompt.

cases.question: What does the author believe is the biggest bottleneck to AI adoption?
cases.answer: Evaluation; the author believes building reliable evaluation pipelines will unlock many new applications.

evidence.quote: I believe that evaluation is the biggest bottleneck to AI adoption. Being able to build reliable evaluation pipelines will unlock many new applications.

cases.question: According to what some teams told the author, in what format does data work best for their retrieval systems?
cases.answer: Some teams said their retrieval systems work best when the data is organized in a question-and-answer format.

evidence.quote: Some teams have told me that their retrieval systems work best when the data is organized in a question-and-answer format.

cases.question: Why does the author consider semantic caching's value more dubious than other caching techniques?
cases.answer: Because many of its components are prone to failure: it relies on high-quality embeddings, functional vector search, and a reliable similarity metric, and the threshold is hard to set.

evidence.quote: Compared to other caching techniques, semantic caching’s value is more dubious because many of its components are prone to failure. Its success relies on high-quality embeddings, functional vector search, and a reliable similarity metric.

cases.question: As of September 2024, what did Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth charge per image for labeling, according to the book?
cases.answer: 8 cents per image for fewer than 50,000 images, but only 2 cents per image for more than 1 million images.

evidence.quote: For example, as of September 2024, Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth charges 8 cents per image for labeling fewer than 50,000 images, but only 2 cents per image for labeling more than 1 million images.

cases.question: How many queries does the PAIR attack often need to produce a jailbreak?
cases.answer: Fewer than twenty queries.

evidence.quote: In their experiment, PAIR often requires fewer than twenty queries to produce a jailbreak.

cases.question: How many bits does the TF32 format actually occupy?
cases.answer: TF32 actually has 19 bits, not 32.

evidence.quote: Note that usually the number at the end of a format’s name signifies how many bits it occupies, but TF32 actually has 19 bits, not 32 bits.

cases.question: In the LIMA study cited by the book, in what percentage of cases were the finetuned model's answers equivalent or strictly preferred to GPT-4?
cases.answer: 43% of cases, as judged by human annotators, using 1,000 carefully curated prompts and responses.

evidence.quote: Similarly, “LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment” (Zhou et al., 2023) shows that a 65B-parameter Llama model, finetuned with 1,000 carefully curated prompts and responses, can produce answers that are either equivalent or strictly preferred to GPT-4 in 43% of cases, as judged by human annotators.

cases.question: Anthropic is cited both for a chunk-contextualization technique and for prompt caching. How long is the context Anthropic generates per chunk, and what maximum cost savings does its prompt caching promise?
cases.answer: The generated context is usually 50-100 tokens per chunk, and Anthropic's prompt caching promises up to 90% cost savings (and up to 75% latency reduction).

evidence.quote: Anthropic used AI models to generate a short context, usually 50-100 tokens, that explains the chunk and its relationship to the original document.
Anthropic offers prompt caching that promises up to 90% cost savings (the longer the cached context, the higher the savings) and up to 75% latency reduction.

cases.question: How many tokens did Meta train Llama 3 on, and how does Llama 3's vocabulary size compare with Llama 2's in the book's dimension table?
cases.answer: Llama 3 was trained on 15 trillion tokens, and its vocabulary is 128K versus 32K for Llama 2.

evidence.quote: Meta used increasingly larger datasets to train their Llama models:
15 trillion tokens for Llama 3

cases.question: How many tools did Chameleon use and how much did it improve the best published few-shot result on ScienceQA, compared with how many tools Toolformer learned?
cases.answer: Chameleon used 13 tools and improved ScienceQA by 11.37%, whereas Toolformer finetuned GPT-J to learn five tools.

evidence.quote: On ScienceQA, a science question answering benchmark, Chameleon improves the best published few-shot result by 11.37%.
For example, Toolformer (Schick et al., 2023) finetuned GPT-J to learn five tools. Chameleon (Lu et al., 2023) uses 13 tools.

cases.question: On the current-events QA study cited in the book, what score did Mistral-7B reach with RAG, and how large can vector database spending get relative to model API spending?
cases.answer: Mistral-7B scored 0.875 with base model + RAG (vs 0.481 base); vector database spending can be one-fifth or even half of model API spending.

evidence.quote: It’s not uncommon to see a company’s vector database spending be one-fifth or even half of their spending on model APIs.

cases.question: The book's semantic cache stores embeddings of cached queries in a vector database. If those embeddings came from OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large, how many dimensions would each have?
cases.answer: 3,072 dimensions.

cases.question: What similarity threshold does the author recommend for semantic caching?
cases.answer: The document does not specify a threshold value.

cases.question: When customizing a language model, which method does the author say should shape how responses look, and which should supply the information in them?
cases.answer: Finetuning is for form (syntax and style); RAG is for facts.

evidence.quote: In short, finetuning is for form, and RAG is for facts.

cases.question: If a person fixes the code an assistant wrote, how can that correction be turned into a signal for aligning the system with what people want?
cases.answer: Each user edit becomes a preference example: the original response is the losing response and the edited one is the winning response.

evidence.quote: Each user edit makes up a preference example, with the original generated response being the losing response and the edited response being the winning response.

cases.question: Which unglamorous chore did one of the people who started a well-known AI lab say pays off the most relative to the credit it earns?
cases.answer: Greg Brockman (OpenAI co-founder) said manual inspection of data has probably the highest value-to-prestige ratio in machine learning.

evidence.quote: Greg Brockman, an OpenAI co-founder, tweeted: “Manual inspection of data has probably the highest value-to-prestige ratio of any activity in machine learning.”

cases.question: Some say crafting instructions for chatbots isn't a real discipline. How does the author think that work should be carried out?
cases.answer: Prompt experiments should be conducted with the same rigor as any ML experiment, with systematic experimentation and evaluation.

evidence.quote: Prompt experiments should be conducted with the same rigor as any ML experiment, with systematic experimentation and evaluation.
